_meta.name: DJBA
_meta.author: Michael Sokoloff
_meta.description: Comprehensive dictionary of Babylonian Talmud Aramaic - essential for Talmud study
_meta.note: Academic Tier 1 - Primary source for Talmudic Aramaic

אמר.fullDefinition: Peal: 1. to say; 2. to tell; 3. to mean; Ithpeel: to be said

תנא.definition: Tanna, Mishnaic sage, one who teaches
תנא.fullDefinition: 1. Tannaitic sage (pre-Amoraic); 2. teacher of Mishnah/Baraita; 3. reciter of traditions

תני.fullDefinition: Peal: to teach, recite (Mishnah/Baraita); forms: תנן (we learned), תניא (it was taught)
תני.talmudic_usage: Technical term for citing Tannaitic sources
תני.examples: תנן - we learned in the Mishnah; תניא - it was taught in a Baraita

תנן.fullDefinition: First person plural perfect of תני; introduces Mishnaic citations
תנן.examples: תנן התם - we learned there (in the Mishnah)

תניא.fullDefinition: Third person singular passive of תני; introduces Baraita citations
תניא.talmudic_usage: Formula for quoting Baraita (external Tannaitic teaching)
תניא.examples: תניא נמי הכי - it was also taught thus

אמורא.fullDefinition: Sage of the Amoraic period (post-Mishnah); interpreter of Mishnah
אמורא.examples: אמוראי דארעא דישראל - Amoraim of the Land of Israel

גמרא.fullDefinition: 1. the Gemara (Amoraic commentary on Mishnah); 2. Talmudic learning; 3. tradition
גמרא.examples: גמרא גמירי - they learned by tradition

משנה.fullDefinition: 1. the Mishnah; 2. a specific Mishnaic teaching; Aramaic: מתניתא/מתניתין

ברייתא.fullDefinition: Tannaitic teaching not included in the Mishnah; 'external' teaching
ברייתא.examples: תניא בברייתא - it was taught in a Baraita

הלכה.fullDefinition: 1. halacha, Jewish law; 2. legal ruling; 3. final decision
הלכה.examples: הלכתא כוותיה - the halacha is according to him

מילתא.fullDefinition: 1. word; 2. matter, thing; 3. statement; 4. case, situation

סברא.examples: סברא הוא - it is logical reasoning

קשיא.fullDefinition: 1. difficulty (remains unresolved); 2. objection; technical term for unresolved contradiction

תיובתא.fullDefinition: Decisive refutation that defeats an opinion (stronger than קשיא)
תיובתא.examples: תיובתא דרב - refutation of Rav's opinion

פירכא.fullDefinition: Objection or refutation (especially to a kal vachomer argument)
פירכא.examples: איכא למיפרך - there is room to object

טעמא.examples: מאי טעמא - what is the reason?

דינא.fullDefinition: 1. law; 2. judgment, verdict; 3. court case; 4. justice
דינא.examples: דינא דמלכותא דינא - the law of the kingdom is the law

עלמא.fullDefinition: 1. world; 2. everyone, people in general; 3. eternity
עלמא.examples: כולי עלמא - everyone; האי עלמא - this world

גברא.examples: גברא רבה - great man; האי גברא - this man

ביתא.fullDefinition: 1. house; 2. home; 3. household; 4. temple (בי כנישתא = synagogue)
ביתא.examples: בי רב - the house/school of Rav

ממונא.fullDefinition: 1. money; 2. property; 3. monetary matters (vs. איסורא ritual matters)

איסורא.fullDefinition: 1. prohibition; 2. forbidden thing; 3. ritual/religious matters (vs. ממונא monetary)
איסורא.examples: דיני איסור והיתר - laws of forbidden and permitted

קמא.examples: תנא קמא - the first Tanna; לישנא קמא - the first version

בתרא.examples: בבא בתרא - the Last Gate; לישנא בתרא - the latter version

רבא.examples: גברא רבא - great man; תלמידא רבא - great student

השתא.examples: השתא דאתית להכי - now that you have come to this

התם.definition: there, in that place, in that case
התם.fullDefinition: 1. there; 2. in that Mishnah/source; 3. in that case
התם.examples: התם אמרינן - there we say; מאי שנא התם - what is different there?

הכא.definition: here, in this place, in this case
הכא.fullDefinition: 1. here; 2. in this Mishnah/source; 3. in this case
הכא.examples: הכא נמי - here also; מאי שנא הכא - what is different here?

לקמן.fullDefinition: Below/later in the text (opposite of לעיל)

לעיל.fullDefinition: Above/earlier in the text (opposite of לקמן)

נמי.fullDefinition: Also, too, likewise (very common in Talmud)
נמי.examples: הכא נמי - here also; תניא נמי הכי - it was also taught thus

אלא.examples: אלא מאי - but what then?; אלא הכי קאמר - but rather he means this

דילמא.examples: דילמא אתי למיטעי - lest one come to err

למאי.examples: למאי נפקא מינה - what practical difference does it make?

היכי.examples: היכי דמי - how is it?; what case are we discussing?

מאי.examples: מאי טעמא - what is the reason?; מאי שנא - what is different?

היינו.definition: that is, this is the same as
היינו.fullDefinition: 1. that is; 2. this is identical to; 3. explains equivalence
היינו.examples: היינו הך - that is the same thing

פשיטא.fullDefinition: It is obvious/self-evident (often introduces objection: why state the obvious?)
פשיטא.examples: פשיטא! - Obviously!; מהו דתימא...קא משמע לן - you might have thought...it teaches us

קמשמע לן.definition: it teaches us, it informs us
קמשמע לן.fullDefinition: It teaches us (response to פשיטא objection)
קמשמע לן.examples: קמ״ל - abbreviation; it teaches us something not obvious

מנא הני מילי.fullDefinition: From where do we derive this? (asks for scriptural source)
מנא הני מילי.examples: מנה״מ דכתיב - from where? as it is written...

שאני.fullDefinition: It is different (introduces distinction to resolve contradiction)
שאני.examples: התם שאני - there it is different (because...)

תיקו.fullDefinition: The question remains unresolved; traditionally: תשבי יתרץ קושיות ואבעיות

לישנא.examples: לישנא קמא - first version; לישנא אחרינא - another version

סתמא.examples: סתם משנה - anonymous Mishnah; סתמא דתלמודא - the anonymous voice of the Talmud

אי.examples: אי הכי - if so; אי נמי - or also

אף על גב.examples: אע״ג דאמר - even though he said

כיון.fullDefinition: 1. since, because; 2. when, as soon as
כיון.examples: כיון דאמר - since he said; כיון שאמר - when he said

משום.definition: because of, on account of, in the name of
משום.fullDefinition: 1. because of; 2. on account of; 3. in the name of (attribution)
משום.examples: משום רבי - in the name of Rabbi; משום דאמר - because he said

למימרא.definition: is it to say? does this mean?
למימרא.fullDefinition: Is this to say? Does this imply? (introduces inference for examination)
למימרא.examples: למימרא דכולי עלמא - is it to say that everyone...

מכלל.examples: מכלל דאמר - from this we infer that he said

מאן.examples: מאן דאמר - whoever says; מאן תנא - who is the Tanna?

אידך.fullDefinition: The other, another (often in אידך גיסא - the other side)
אידך.examples: אידך גיסא - on the other hand; ואידך - and the other (sage)?

חד.examples: חד אמר - one said; חד מינייהו - one of them

תרי.examples: תרי גברי - two men; תרווייהו - both of them

תלת.examples: תלתא - three; תלת מילי - three things

ארבע.examples: ארבע מילי - four things; ארבעה - four

פלוגתא.examples: פלוגתא דרבי ורבנן - dispute between Rabbi and the Sages

מחלוקת.fullDefinition: Dispute, controversy (often במחלוקת שנויה - it is taught in dispute)
מחלוקת.examples: מחלוקת ואחר כך סתם - dispute and then anonymous = halakha follows anonymous

יליף.fullDefinition: To derive (a law), learn from (a source); Peal participle used
יליף.examples: מנא יליף - from where does he derive?; יליף לה מהכא - he derives it from here

נפקא מינה.definition: practical difference, what comes out of it
נפקא מינה.fullDefinition: What practical difference/result comes from it
נפקא מינה.examples: מאי נפקא מינה - what practical difference does it make?

דכולי עלמא.fullDefinition: According to everyone's opinion, universally agreed
דכולי עלמא.examples: דכולי עלמא לא פליגי - according to everyone there is no dispute

נפק.fullDefinition: Peal: to go out, exit, leave, emerge. Aphel (אפיק/תפיק): to bring out, remove, derive. Pe-Nun verb (פ״נ): the initial נ assimilates in Aphel forms.
נפק.talmudic_usage: Extremely common. נפקא מינה = practical difference; נפקא לן = we derive; לאפוקי = to exclude
נפק.examples: מאי נפקא מינה - what practical difference?; תפיקו - you shall bring out; לאפוקי מאי - to exclude what?

אפיק.definition: to bring out, remove (Aphel of נפק)
אפיק.fullDefinition: Aphel (causative) of נפק: to bring out, remove, derive, exclude. Common in halachic discourse.
אפיק.talmudic_usage: Used for exclusion in legal reasoning
אפיק.examples: לאפוקי - to exclude; אפיק ליה - he removed it

תפיק.definition: you will bring out, it will bring out (Aphel of נפק)
תפיק.fullDefinition: Aphel imperfect of נפק: 2ms/3fs 'you/it will bring out'. Common in Biblical quotations in Talmud.
תפיק.examples: לא תפיקו - you shall not bring out

מפיק.definition: one who brings out, bringing out (Aphel participle of נפק)
מפיק.fullDefinition: Aphel participle of נפק: one who brings out, derives. Also grammatical term for mappiq (dot in final ה).

לאפוקי.definition: to exclude, to the exclusion of
לאפוקי.fullDefinition: Infinitive of Aphel נפק with preposition: to exclude, to the exclusion of. Extremely common in Talmudic reasoning.
לאפוקי.examples: לאפוקי מאי - to exclude what?; לאפוקי רבי יהודה - to exclude Rabbi Yehuda's opinion

נפקא.definition: it goes out, it derives (3fs of נפק)
נפקא.fullDefinition: Third person feminine singular of נפק. In Talmudic usage: 'it derives', 'the result is'.
נפקא.talmudic_usage: Used in derivational contexts - נפקא לן = we derive
נפקא.examples: נפקא לן מהכא - we derive from here; נפקא מינה - the practical difference

עבד.fullDefinition: Peal: to do, make, work. Ithpael: to be done. Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew עשה.
עבד.talmudic_usage: מאי עביד - what does he do?; עובדא הוה - there was an incident
עבד.examples: עביד - he does; הכי עבדינן - thus we do

עביד.fullDefinition: Active participle of עבד: doing, making. Very common form.
עביד.examples: עביד הכי - he does thus; מאי עביד - what is he doing?

אזל.fullDefinition: Peal: to go, walk, proceed, depart. Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew הלך.
אזל.examples: אזל - he went; אזיל - he goes

אתא.fullDefinition: Peal: to come, arrive, approach. Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew בא.
אתא.talmudic_usage: Common in narrative and derivation (מהכא אתי - from here it comes)
אתא.examples: אתא - he came; אתי למימר - it comes to say

יהב.fullDefinition: Peal: to give, place, put. Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew נתן.
יהב.examples: יהב ליה - he gave to him; יהבינן - we give

נסב.fullDefinition: Peal: to take, take in marriage, receive. Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew לקח.
נסב.talmudic_usage: נסיב איתתא - he married a woman
נסב.examples: נסב - he took; נסיב - he takes/marries

חזא.fullDefinition: Peal: to see, perceive, understand. Common in TA (תא חזי - come and see).
חזא.talmudic_usage: תא חזי - come and see (introducing proof)

ידע.fullDefinition: Peal: to know, understand. Very common in Talmudic argumentation.
ידע.talmudic_usage: ידעינן - we know; מנא ידעינן - from where do we know?
ידע.examples: ידע - he knows; לא ידענא - I don't know

בעא.fullDefinition: Peal: to seek, ask, request. Common in בעא מיניה (he asked him) and איבעיא להו (they asked).
בעא.talmudic_usage: בעא מיניה - he asked him; איבעיא להו - it was asked
בעא.examples: בעא - he sought/asked; מיבעיא - it is asked

יתב.fullDefinition: Peal: to sit, dwell. Aphel (אותיב): to seat, cause to sit, raise an objection (figuratively 'seat' a problem).
יתב.talmudic_usage: יתיב וקאמר - he sat and said; מותיב - he raised an objection
יתב.examples: יתיב - he sits; מותבינן - we raise an objection

קום.fullDefinition: Peal: to stand, rise, exist. Common in קאי (he stands) and קיימא לן (it is established for us).
קום.talmudic_usage: קיימא לן - we hold (as established law)
קום.examples: קאי - he stands; קיימא לן - we hold

סבר.definition: to think, hold, be of opinion
סבר.fullDefinition: Peal: to think, hold an opinion, reason. Fundamental verb for expressing legal opinions.
סבר.talmudic_usage: סבר לה כוותיה - he holds like him; סבירא ליה - he is of the opinion
סבר.examples: סבר - he thinks; מאי סבר - what does he think?

קרי.fullDefinition: Peal: to read, call, recite. Common for citing Scripture and Mishnah.
קרי.talmudic_usage: קרי ליה - he calls it; קרינן ביה - we read in it (apply the verse)
קרי.examples: קרי - he reads/calls; קרינן - we read

עאל.fullDefinition: Peal: to enter, go in. Opposite of נפק (go out).
עאל.talmudic_usage: עייל ונפיק - he goes in and out
עאל.examples: עאל - he entered; עייל - he enters

שמע.fullDefinition: Peal: to hear, listen, accept. Common in תא שמע (come and hear) introducing proof.
שמע.talmudic_usage: תא שמע - come and hear (introducing proof text)
שמע.examples: שמע מינה - learn from this; תא שמע - come and hear

אמרי.definition: they say, we say (plural of אמר)
אמרי.fullDefinition: Plural form of אמר: they say, we say. Very common in Talmudic discourse.
אמרי.talmudic_usage: אמרי לה - some say; אמרי במערבא - they say in the West (Israel)
אמרי.examples: אמרי - they say; איכא דאמרי - some say

הוה.fullDefinition: Peal: to be, exist, happen, become. Fundamental existential verb in Aramaic.
הוה.talmudic_usage: עובדא הוה - there was an incident; הכי הוה - thus it was
הוה.examples: הוה אמינא - I would have said; מהו דתימא - what might you have thought

אית.definition: there is, there are; to have (with ל)
אית.fullDefinition: Existential particle: there is/are. With dative: to have (אית ליה = he has).
אית.talmudic_usage: אית ליה - he has; אית דאמרי - there are those who say
אית.examples: אית ליה - he has; אית לן למימר - we can say

לית.definition: there is not, there are not; to not have
לית.fullDefinition: Negative existential particle: there is not. With dative: to not have (לית ליה = he doesn't have).
לית.talmudic_usage: לית ליה - he doesn't have; לית הלכתא - the halacha is not
לית.examples: לית ליה - he doesn't have; ליתא - it is not so

גמר.fullDefinition: Peal: to learn, derive (by gezera shava or other hermeneutic); to complete. Root of גמרא.
גמר.talmudic_usage: גמירי - we learned by tradition; גזירה שוה גמיר - he derives by gezera shava
גמר.examples: גמר מיניה - he learned from him; גמרינן - we learn
